# Synthetic practice: learn the workflow

Start after [Required setup](../../00-setup.qmd). The 120 fictional genes and groups A and B were constructed for teaching; do not give them biological names or treat their statistical signals as findings about an organism.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Our question

Which fictional genes have different model-estimated counts in group B compared with group A, and how can we verify and explain the outputs?
:::

By the end you will match 12 sample IDs across two files, check the design and counts, run the supplied R workflow, verify A01 independently, explain the sign of a fold change, and write a short report.

| Lesson | Task |
|---|---|
| [Preview](01-see-the-result.qmd) | Learn what the PCA, count summary and gene table represent |
| [Meet](02-meet-the-data.qmd) | Inspect samples, gene counts and group labels |
| [Check](03-check-the-inputs.qmd) | Validate format, IDs, replicates and contrast |
| [Run](04-run-the-analysis.qmd) | Save the DESeq2 table, PCA and run record |
| [Verify](05-verify-and-explain.qmd) | Independently calculate A01's count summary |
| [Write](06-export-the-report.qmd) | Report evidence, interpretation and limits |

Run shell commands in the terminal **from the main project folder**. Run R expressions in the R console or in a saved `.R` script. Quarto rendering displays the guide; it does not execute the analysis.

**Before continuing:** explain why an A/B result in invented data cannot be presented as a biological discovery.
